name: Arab socialism
summary: Arab socialism treats socialism as a national, non-Marxist means to Arab renewal and unity: state ownership of key industry, land reform and social services, with private property kept within limits and class struggle rejected in favour of national solidarity. It is anti-imperialist, non-aligned, hostile to Zionism, secular-leaning while respecting Islam, and in power became strong-executive, one-party rule.
scope: Mainstream mid-20th-century Arab socialism as the defining sources present it: a nationalist, non-Marxist socialism that rejects class struggle, in its two strands: Michel Aflaq and Salah al-Din al-Bitar's Ba'th (Fi Sabil al-Ba'th; the 1947 party constitution) and Nasser's Egypt (1962 National Charter, Arab Socialist Union), which the sources name as its parties and regimes (s6, s2, s9, s7). It excludes Marxist-Leninist Arab communism, Islamic socialism proper, and Ba'thism or Nasserism as wholes except where they state the socialist programme; later Saddam-era, Assadist and Qaddafist regimes count only where the sources tie them to the ideology.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The 1947 constitution has a single state bank issuing the currency.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: The 1947 constitution guarantees a job and a decent wage.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: The 1947 constitution caps individual land holdings rather than making all land state property.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: Arab socialism supported liberation movements and opposed imperialism (Irani).

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The 1947 constitution calls freedom of art sacred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The 1947 constitution has a single state bank issuing the currency.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The 1947 constitution makes health care, education and jobs a state guarantee.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The 1947 constitution calls colonialism a crime and backs peoples fighting for their freedom, which rules out any right to rule them.

class-collaboration.rationale: Ba'th and Nasserism rejected class struggle and stressed national unity across classes.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Aflaq rejected class analysis and historical materialism (Asfar), and Arab socialism rejected Marxism and class struggle (Irani).

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The Ba'th programme treats Arab unity as a single nation divided by imperial partition, so borders drawn by colonial treaties carry no binding force.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The 1947 constitution calls colonialism a crime and abrogates treaties that harm Arab sovereignty.

conscription.rationale: Art. 8 of the 1947 constitution makes military service compulsory.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The 1947 program calls the executive responsible to the people under a representative regime, though practice differed.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The 1947 constitution guarantees every citizen a job and a decent wage, and free health care.

decide-locally.rationale: The 1947 constitution calls for decentralized administration within a single Arab state.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The 1947 constitution gives Arab women full civic rights and the Ba'th called for sexual equality.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The 1947 constitution abolishes foreign concessions and puts large industry under the state.

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: The 1947 constitution provides free health care and free education.

free-trade.rationale: The program places foreign and domestic trade under direct state control and bans foreign concessions.

gradual-change.rationale: The 1947 constitution calls the party revolutionary, and Aflaq accepted revolution (inqilab).

harm-principle.rationale: The program values freedoms as sacred but state limits them by national interest.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The constitution forbids exploiting others' labour and calls for a fair redistribution of wealth.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Abolishing foreign concessions and Nasser's nationalizations show political independence linked to economic transformation.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Irani records Arab socialism as anti-Zionist.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Union of all Arabs, one language-family people, is the central aim.

land-redistribution.rationale: Encyclopedia of the Modern Middle East: Arab socialism carried out land reform and redistribution; the 1947 constitution caps land holdings.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The constitution defines Arabs as those who speak Arabic and live, or aspire to live, on Arab soil, so language is part of the definition, not all of it.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The 1947 constitution puts public utilities under state management; it names the state, not local bodies.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Aflaq rejected economic and historical materialism but accepted economic factors as one influence (Asfar).

national-rebirth.rationale: The Ba'th's name means renaissance or resurrection and its core aim is Arab national rebirth after decline.

national-resource-control.rationale: The 1947 constitution puts natural resources under the state and abolishes foreign concessions.

national-self-determination.rationale: The constitution backs peoples fighting for freedom and a single Arab state for the Arab nation; it states no general rule for every people.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The 1947 constitution gives the state health care, education, utilities, large industry, trade and the currency.

no-central-bank.rationale: The 1947 constitution has a single state bank issuing the currency.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The 1947 constitution fights confessional, tribal and racial fanaticism.

one-party-rule.rationale: The National Charter made the Arab Socialist Union the sole legal party in Egypt (LoC).

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Ba'th ideology is a romantic, spiritual nationalism centred on Arab cultural renaissance.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The 1947 constitution has the state encourage marriage and having more children.

property-fundamental.rationale: Art. 9 protects property and inheritance as natural rights only within the limits of national interest, so it can be overridden.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Art. 9 holds property and inheritance inviolable only within the national interest, and the constitution forbids exploiting others' labour.

public-ownership.rationale: Art. 4 of the 1947 constitution puts utilities, natural resources, large industry and transport under state management; the Nasser-era National Charter nationalized large industry and banks (LoC).

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The program condemns racial fanaticism and colonialism.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The state controls trade, abolishes foreign concessions and takes over large undertakings, a stronger stance than regulation.

religion-illusion.rationale: Aflaq rejected the disparagement of religion found in Marxism (Asfar).

religious-nation.rationale: The constitution defines the Arab nation by language and land, not religion.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Art. 6 seeks union of all Arabs divided by colonial borders.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: The 1947 constitution calls the party revolutionary, and Aflaq accepted revolution (inqilab).

school-vouchers.rationale: The 1947 constitution makes education free and state-run and abolishes private and foreign schools.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The program says the executive is responsible to the people under constitutional rule.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Aflaq held that Arab renewal has a spiritual side and the regime respected Islam alongside material development.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The 1947 constitution has the state run large industry and carry out a full industrialization programme.

state-harmful.rationale: The ideology rests on a strong state directing the economy and unifying the Arab nation.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Isaac and Irani both record non-alignment between the Cold War blocs.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The 1947 constitution provides health care and education free to all, not limited to the poor.

unions-good.rationale: The 1947 constitution provides for free unions of workers and peasants.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 1947 constitution provides free health care.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers were to share in wages and management under the 1947 program, though under state oversight.

notes: The Ba'th (parliamentary rhetoric, pan-Arab party) and Nasserism (sole-party presidency) differ on democracy; answers use only what the sources state. Positions the 1947 Ba'th constitution, Isaac, Irani, the LoC study and Asfar do not state are null.
